entries.title: Fixes commonly misheard phrases like 'bear with me', 'peace of mind', 'per se', and 'free rein'
highlights: Repairs everyday phrases that speech recognizers often spell with the wrong homophone, turning 'bare with me', 'bare in mind', 'piece of mind', 'for all intensive purposes', 'per say', 'mute point', 'free reign', 'baited breath', 'all of the sudden', and 'trail of thought' into 'bear with me', 'bear in mind', 'peace of mind', 'for all intents and purposes', 'per se', 'moot point', 'free rein', 'bated breath', 'all of a sudden', and 'train of thought'.
Fixes 'peaked my interest' and 'peeked my curiosity' to 'piqued my interest' and 'piqued my curiosity'.

entries.title: Cleans up 'or better yet' and 'actually, forget that' mid-sentence self-corrections
highlights: When you upgrade an idea or time mid-sentence with 'or better yet' or 'actually, forget that' ('Let us meet at 3 p.m., or better yet, 4 p.m.' or 'Make the tone formal, actually, forget that, keep it casual and friendly'), GeminiFlow keeps only your updated instruction.
Recognizes direct action starters like 'just give me', 'keep it', and 'please' when replacing an earlier draft instruction.

entries.title: Cleans up rambling connector collisions like 'so which it makes sense' and 'which is why that'
highlights: Smooths out overlapping connectors when thinking out loud, turning 'so which it makes sense' and 'which it makes sense' into ', which makes sense' and 'which makes sense'.
Simplifies 'which is why that', 'even though that', 'because then so', 'and then so', and 'most of the times' into 'which is why', 'even though', 'so', 'and so', and 'most of the time'.

entries.title: Removes filler 'like' around 'for example', 'and then like', and '-ly' adverbs and frames 'let us say'
highlights: Removes filler 'like' next to example phrases and transitions ('like for example', 'for example like', 'like for instance', 'like let us say', 'and then like I restarted') and before adverbs such as 'specifically', 'especially', 'personally', 'essentially', 'ideally', 'normally', 'usually', 'clearly', and 'hopefully'.
Adds natural commas around 'let us say' inside 'when' or 'if' thoughts ('when let us say I change my mind' becomes 'when, let us say, I change my mind').

entries.title: Repairs clipped first words like 'ere is an', 'hat is why', and 'ecause' when pressing to talk
highlights: Restores the missing first letters when you begin speaking a split second before pressing the hotkey, turning clipped starts like 'ere's an independent reviewer', 'ere is a', 'hat's why', 'ecause', 'lso,', and 'nd also' into 'There's an independent reviewer', 'There is a', 'That's why', 'Because', 'Also,', and 'And also'.

entries.title: Formats 'ChatGPT', knowledge-work apps, and compounds like 'brainstorm', 'workaround', and 'handoff'
highlights: Restores proper capitalization on AI and knowledge-work tools including 'ChatGPT' (whether spoken as 'ChatGPT' or 'chat G P T'), 'Midjourney', 'Figma', 'Canva', 'Airtable', 'Zapier', 'Grammarly', 'Calendly', 'DocuSign', 'Dropbox', 'OneDrive', 'SharePoint', 'Evernote', 'Todoist', 'Trello', and 'Asana'.
Joins split planning and workflow nouns such as 'brainstorm', 'brainstorming', 'workaround', 'walkthrough', and 'handoff'.

entries.title: Fixes missing apostrophes in 'im', 'dont', and 'thats' and cleans up 'more better' double comparatives
highlights: Adds missing apostrophes and capitalization to contractions like 'when im saying', 'dont', 'doesnt', 'didnt', 'wont', 'cant', 'isnt', 'thats', 'whats', 'theres', 'youre', 'theyre', and 'ive' ('when im saying 1 pax' becomes 'when I'm saying 1 pax').

Cleans up spoken double comparatives when thinking out loud, turning 'more better', 'more easier', 'more faster', 'more cleaner', 'more clearer', and 'more simpler' into 'better', 'easier', 'faster', 'cleaner', 'clearer', and 'simpler'.

entries.title: Cleans up 'that is not what I meant', 'what I mean is', and 'to put it another way' self-corrections
highlights: When you steer an AI or revise a thought mid-sentence with 'that is not what I meant', 'wait, that is not what I meant', 'what I mean is', or 'to put it another way', GeminiFlow replaces the earlier draft with your clarified instruction.
Works for both short phrase replacements ('Focus on coding, what I mean is, personal conversations') and full clause restarts.

entries.title: Removes filler 'like' after '-ing' action words and at the end of sentences
highlights: Removes filler 'like' after '-ing' action words when collecting your thoughts ('catching like those redundant words', 'putting like the correct punctuation', 'losing like the meaning or changing like my voice', 'collecting like my thoughts'), while keeping real comparisons like 'looking like rain' or 'working like a charm'.
Strips trailing ', like.' filler at the end of a sentence.

entries.title: Re-attaches trailing 'In case...', 'Rather than...', and 'Of putting...' fragments after thinking pauses
highlights: Joins trailing 'In case...', 'Rather than...', 'Instead of...', and 'Even though...' fragments back onto your sentence when a brief pause caused a premature period ('Make sure to do your handoffs and commit frequently. In case tokens run out.' becomes 'Make sure to do your handoffs and commit frequently in case tokens run out.').

Re-attaches trailing 'Of ...-ing' phrases onto questions and statements ('Is this something that you are working on for the upcoming cycles? Of actually putting the correct punctuation.' becomes 'Is this something that you are working on for the upcoming cycles of actually putting the correct punctuation?').

entries.title: Hyphenates 'non-developer' and 'trade-off' and adds question marks to 'if ..., then how ...?' questions
highlights: Adds hyphens to spoken 'non-' words and planning terms such as 'non-developer', 'non-technical', 'non-urgent', 'non-negotiable', 'non-stop', 'non-issue', 'non-starter', 'non-profit', and 'trade-off'.
Adds a question mark when a longer sentence starts with 'if', 'when', or 'because' and pivots into a question like 'because I tend to ramble, then how can my thoughts be collected?'.

entries.title: Fixes stray mid-sentence capitals after thinking pauses like 'run Out of tokens' and 'then How can'
highlights: Lowercases stray capital letters on prepositions and connectors after a brief mid-sentence pause ('until you finish everything or run Out of tokens' becomes 'until you finish everything or run out of tokens').

Adds a natural comma and lowercases the question word when a 'because', 'if', or 'when' thought pivots with 'then' into a question ('because I tend to ramble then How can my thoughts be collected?' becomes 'because I tend to ramble, then how can my thoughts be collected?').

entries.title: Cleans up multi-word clause restarts like 'I was trying to catch the I was trying to test'
highlights: When you start a sentence frame like 'I was trying to...', 'I want to...', 'I am going to...', or 'we need to...', say one or two tentative words, and immediately restart with the same frame ('I was trying to catch the I was trying to test when...'), GeminiFlow collapses the false start while keeping your exact wording.
Preserves intentional repetition and parallel sentences where both clauses are complete thoughts.

entries.title: Cleans up mid-thought verb upgrades like 'is would be', 'to go to keep going', and 'because then now'
highlights: When you soften or refine a verb mid-thought while thinking out loud ('my next request is would be for you' or 'for you to go to keep going'), GeminiFlow keeps the refined phrasing ('my next request would be for you' and 'for you to keep going').

Cleans up stacked rambling transitions such as 'because then now', 'and then now', 'so then now', and 'to would have that it would have' into 'because now', 'and now', 'so now', and 'that it would have'.

entries.title: Removes filler 'like' in 'almost like judge', 'this whole like thread', and 'that is like a challenge'
highlights: Removes filler 'like' when thinking out loud between qualifiers and nouns ('in this whole like thread', 'my biggest like use case', 'a specific like word') and between adverbs and verbs ('you can almost like judge the quality').

Removes discourse filler 'like' before evaluative phrases ('That is like a challenge there', 'It is like a big problem', 'That is like the main reason') while preserving genuine comparisons ('just like I am to you now').

entries.title: Hyphenates everyday personal and workplace modifiers like 'follow-up', 'full-time', and '1-on-1'
highlights: Adds hyphens to common personal and work modifiers before their nouns, including 'follow-up email', 'check-in call', 'full-time role', 'part-time schedule', 'long-term plan', 'short-term goal', 'last-minute change', 'in-person meeting', 'one-way ticket', 'round-trip flight', 'day-to-day work', 'face-to-face chat', 'step-by-step guide', and 'up-to-date schedule'.
Formats 'one on one' or '1 on 1' before meeting and call nouns into '1-on-1' ('our 1-on-1 meeting'), while keeping verb phrases like 'follow up with Sarah' or 'check in at the hotel' unhyphenated.

entries.title: Cleans up 'change that to', 'switch that to', and 'not X, Y' self-corrections
highlights: When you revise an earlier detail mid-sentence with 'change that to', 'switch that to', or 'actually make it' ('Book it for 7 p.m., change that to 8 p.m.' or 'I will take 2 coffees, actually make it 3'), GeminiFlow updates the earlier word or number in place.
Cleans up comma-separated 'not X, Y' corrections when you repeat the word you are replacing ('Let us meet on Tuesday, not Tuesday, Wednesday' becomes 'Let us meet on Wednesday').

entries.title: Formats spoken household, cooking, fitness, and '24/7' expressions
highlights: Abbreviates everyday personal, cooking, and fitness measurements after numbers, turning '5 feet 10 inches', '16 ounces', '8 fluid ounces', '2 tablespoons', '1 teaspoon', '2,000 kilocalories', and '120 beats per minute' into '5 ft 10 in', '16 oz', '8 fl oz', '2 tbsp', '1 tsp', '2,000 kcal', and '120 bpm'.
Turns spoken ratio expressions like '24 slash 7' and '50 slash 50' into '24/7' and '50/50'.

entries.title: Formats spoken everyday abbreviations like 'RSVP', 'ASAP', 'FYI', 'ETA', and 'PTO' and group 'pax' ranges
highlights: Turns spoken everyday and workplace abbreviations into uppercase, including 'RSVP', 'ASAP', 'FYI', 'TBD', 'TBA', 'Q&A', 'DIY', 'VIP', 'WFH', 'ETA', 'PTO', and 'OOO'.
Extends 'pax' dining and event count repair to cover numeric ranges and group questions such as 'table for 2 to 3 pax', '10-12 pax', and 'How many pax for dinner?'.

entries.title: Removes filler 'like' before frequency words, everyday verbs, and possessives
highlights: Catches filler 'like' before frequency adverbs ('I like often use', 'we like usually meet on Fridays'), before everyday verbs ('I like need to leave', 'we like want to book a table', 'I like think we should wait', 'I have like never been there'), and after possessives or articles ('my like calendar', 'the like whole thing').
Simplifies redundant connector pairs such as 'but yet', 'and also too', and 'in case if' into 'but', 'and also', and 'in case'.

entries.title: Formats more personal and work email greetings, warm sign-offs, and messaging apps
highlights: Adds paragraph breaks after full-name, family, and role-title email greetings such as 'Hi Sarah Johnson,', 'Dear Hiring Manager,', 'Hi Mom and Dad,', and 'Hey friends,'.

Formats warm personal and professional email sign-offs onto their own lines, including 'Warmly,', 'All the best,', 'Take care,', 'Speak soon,', 'See you soon,', 'With gratitude,', 'Lots of love,', and 'Yours truly,', and recognizes WeChat, Line, Messenger, and Viber for casual chat punctuation.

entries.title: Formats spoken clock times and cleans up two-word conversational restarts
highlights: Turns space-separated spoken clock times and ranges like '3 30 p.m.', '10 15 a.m.', 'at 6 30 tonight', and 'from 2 30 to 3 30 p.m.' into '3:30 p.m.', '10:15 a.m.', 'at 6:30 tonight', and '2:30-3:30 p.m.'.

Collapses mid-sentence restarts when you pause after a short phrase and start over with a new article or preposition ('I want a, I want the corner table' becomes 'I want the corner table' and 'I talked to the, I talked to my manager' becomes 'I talked to my manager').

entries.title: Cleans up 'make it', 'on second thought', and 'you know what' self-corrections
highlights: When you revise a number, time, or day mid-sentence with 'make it' ('I will be there in 10 minutes, make it 15' or 'Table for 2, make it 4'), GeminiFlow updates the earlier number in place.

When you change your mind mid-sentence with 'on second thought' or 'actually, you know what' ('Let us meet on Tuesday, on second thought, let us do Wednesday'), GeminiFlow keeps only your updated plan.

entries.title: Removes more redundant 'like' fillers and stacked sentence connectors
highlights: Catches filler 'like' in everyday speech after prepositions ('at like 3 p.m.', 'in like 5 minutes', 'with like my friends', 'about like the budget'), before action verbs and contractions ('I like went to the store', 'he like can't make it', 'we're like trying to finish'), and after connectors ('if like', 'when like', 'because like').
Keeps genuine uses of 'like' untouched ('I like the new design', 'I would like to schedule a call', 'looks like rain') and simplifies stacked connectors like 'because then so that' into 'so that'.

entries.title: Fixes '1 pax' and '2 pax' dining and group counts and adds question marks to casual questions
highlights: Fixes '1 pax', '2 pax', '4 pax', and 'per pax' when dictated for dining reservations, travel, and events so they no longer transcribe as '1 packs', 'a 1 packs', '2 packs', or 'per packs', while keeping product phrases like '2 packs of gum' intact.

Adds a question mark to casual and work questions such as 'Any chance we can move the call to 4 p.m.?', 'Any thoughts on the proposal?', 'Anyone free for lunch today?', 'Want to grab coffee tomorrow?', and 'Mind if we reschedule?'.

entries.title: Formats more technical slash pairs like 'pub/sub', 'key/value', 'UI/UX', and 'HTTP/2'
highlights: Turns spoken technical slash pairs like 'pub slash sub', 'key slash value', 'request slash response', 'primary slash replica', 'active slash passive', 'producer slash consumer', 'UI slash UX', 'HTTP slash 2', and 'HTTP slash 3' into clean slash expressions.
Expands spoken Git and project folder slash paths to cover 'release/v1.2', 'refactor/audio', 'docs/api', and 'tests/e2e'.

entries.title: Hyphenates AI and systems modifiers and restores casing on AI, database, and testing brands
highlights: Hyphenates spoken technical modifiers before their nouns, including 'fine-tuned model', 'pre-trained weights', 'self-hosted runner', 'thread-safe cache', 'type-safe client', 'zero-copy buffers', 'event-driven pipeline', and 'non-blocking io'.

Restores proper capitalization on AI, database, and developer tool names including 'Anthropic', 'HuggingFace', 'LangChain', 'LlamaIndex', 'DuckDB', 'ClickHouse', 'DynamoDB', 'RabbitMQ', 'Datadog', 'PostHog', 'Playwright', 'Vitest', and 'Turborepo'.

entries.title: Formats spoken Asia-Pacific currencies, inequality symbols, and '10x' multipliers
highlights: Turns spoken currency amounts like '500 Hong Kong dollars', '80 New Zealand dollars', '1,000 New Taiwan dollars', '5,000 Indian rupees', and '10,000 Korean won' into 'HK$500', 'NZ$80', 'NT$1,000', '₹5,000', and '₩10,000'.

Formats spoken math comparisons and multipliers before numbers, turning 'greater than or equal to 95 percent', 'less than or equal to 100 milliseconds', and '10 x speedup' into '≥95%', '≤100 ms', and '10x speedup'.

entries.title: Formats spoken bold, italics, curly braces, and angle brackets
highlights: Wraps phrases in Markdown bold or italics when you say 'bold ... end bold' or 'italic ... end italic' ('Make this bold high priority end bold' becomes 'Make this **high priority**').
Wraps template variables and tags in curly braces or angle brackets when you say 'open curly brace ... close curly brace' or 'open angle bracket ... close angle bracket'.

entries.title: Formats spoken Markdown headings and checkbox task lists
highlights: Turns spoken headings at the start of a line like 'Heading 1: Quarterly roadmap' or 'Heading 2 key milestones' into '# Quarterly roadmap' and '## Key milestones'.
Formats spoken task items when you say 'checkbox item ... next checkbox ...' or 'todo item ... next todo ...' into Markdown '- [ ] ' checklists.

entries.title: Cleans up 'let me correct that' and 'correction' mid-sentence fixes
highlights: When you correct yourself mid-sentence with 'let me correct that' or a comma-separated 'correction' ('The meeting is on Tuesday, let me correct that, Wednesday at 2 p.m.' or 'We shipped 12 builds today, correction, 15 builds'), GeminiFlow replaces the earlier detail automatically.
Leaves normal uses of the word 'correction' in everyday sentences like 'Make a small correction to the file' untouched.

entries.title: Joins split software compound words like 'frontend', 'backend', 'runtime', and 'timeout'
highlights: Joins split technical nouns like 'frontend', 'backend', 'runtime', 'timeout', 'rollback', and 'fallback' when dictated in software phrases, while keeping everyday verb phrases like 'roll back the changes' or 'front end of the train' as separate words.
Combines common two-part engineering terms including 'dataset', 'firewall', 'hostname', 'username', 'filename', 'breakpoint', 'checkpoint', 'deadlock', 'payload', and 'backlog'.

entries.title: Formats spoken quotation marks, parentheses, and square brackets
highlights: Wraps phrases in quotes when you say 'quote ... unquote' or 'open quote ... close quote' ('Set status to quote ready for review unquote' becomes 'Set status to "ready for review"').
Wraps spoken asides and tags in parentheses or square brackets when you say 'open paren ... close paren' or 'open bracket ... close bracket'.

entries.title: Formats spoken aspect ratios, video resolutions, and metric units
highlights: Turns spoken display aspect ratios and video resolutions like '16 by 9', '21 by 9', '4 by 3 aspect ratio', '10 80 p', and '4 k video' into '16:9', '21:9', '4:3 aspect ratio', '1080p', and '4K video'.

Abbreviates spoken metric weight, length, and volume units after numbers, turning '500 milligrams', '2.5 kilograms', '15 millimeters', '30 centimeters', '5 kilometers', and '250 milliliters' into '500 mg', '2.5 kg', '15 mm', '30 cm', '5 km', and '250 mL'.

entries.title: Formats more command-line flags and keeps multi-sentence prose capitalized in code editors
highlights: Turns multi-word and single-dash command flags like 'git merge dash dash ff only', 'docker build dash dash no cache', 'go test dash v', 'tail dash f', and 'kill dash 9' into 'git merge --ff-only', 'docker build --no-cache', 'go test -v', 'tail -f', and 'kill -9'.
Preserves capitalization and periods on multi-sentence notes starting with words like 'Make sure' or 'Go ahead' inside code editors while still formatting single-line terminal commands.

entries.title: Keeps capitalization on bullet list items and cleans up dictation inside quotes
highlights: When you start dictating after a bullet or task list marker like '- ', '* ', or '- [ ] ', GeminiFlow keeps the first word of the list item capitalized instead of lowercasing it.
When you place your cursor inside quotation marks mid-sentence, GeminiFlow leaves out the extra period and trailing space before the closing quote.

entries.title: Formats spoken email Subject lines and preserves dotted arguments in terminal commands
highlights: Turns spoken email headers like 'Subject colon quarterly roadmap update. Hi Sarah, thanks for the notes.' into a clean 'Subject: Quarterly roadmap update' line followed by a blank line before the greeting.
Keeps terminal commands lowercase and removes the trailing period even when arguments contain dotted filenames or paths like 'git add main.m' or 'python3 tests/run_tests.py'.

entries.title: Formats spoken 'plus or minus', powers, and area, volume, and speed units
highlights: Turns spoken expressions like 'plus or minus 5 percent' and '10 to the power of 6' into '±5%' and '10^6'.

Abbreviates spoken area, volume, and speed units after numbers, turning '120 square meters', '1,500 square feet', '300 cubic meters', '65 miles per hour', and '105 kilometers per hour' into '120 m²', '1,500 sq ft', '300 m³', '65 mph', and '105 km/h'.

entries.title: Formats spoken code backticks and hex color codes
highlights: Wraps spoken inline code in backticks, turning 'backtick main dot m backtick' and 'backtick max underscore retries backtick' into '`main.m`' and '`max_retries`'.
Turns spoken hex color codes like 'hash 3 8 d c 8 2', 'hex f f 5 7 3 3', and 'hash f f f' into '#38DC82', '#FF5733', and '#FFF'.

entries.title: Formats spoken HTTP status codes like '404 error', 'HTTP 503', and '200 OK'
highlights: Turns spoken web status codes in error and response phrases like 'four oh four error', 'HTTP five oh three service unavailable', 'five oh two bad gateway', and 'two hundred okay' into '404 error', 'HTTP 503 service unavailable', '502 bad gateway', and '200 OK'.
Leaves normal numbers in everyday sentences like 'five hundred people in room four oh four' untouched.

entries.title: Cleans up 'let me rephrase' and 'let me start over' self-corrections and higher ordinals
highlights: When you change your mind mid-sentence with 'let me rephrase', 'let me rephrase that', or 'let me start over', GeminiFlow removes the earlier draft and keeps only your revised sentence or clause.
Expands spoken ordinal number self-corrections through 'thirteenth' to 'thirtieth' ('On the thirteenth floor, wait, fifteenth floor' becomes 'On the fifteenth floor').

entries.title: Formats spoken Canadian, Australian, Singapore, and Swiss currencies and hardware units
highlights: Turns spoken currency amounts like '50 Canadian dollars', '80 Australian dollars', '100 Singapore dollars', and '2.5 million Swiss francs' into 'CA$50', 'A$80', 'S$100', and 'CHF 2.5 million'.
Abbreviates spoken hardware, battery, and audio measurements after numbers, turning '120 hertz', '96 watts', '5,000 milliamp hours', and '24 decibels' into '120 Hz', '96 W', '5,000 mAh', and '24 dB'.

entries.title: Formats spoken Git branch names and single-dash command flags
highlights: Turns spoken Git remote and branch references like 'origin slash main', 'upstream slash main', 'feature slash oauth', and 'hotfix slash login' into 'origin/main', 'upstream/main', 'feature/oauth', and 'hotfix/login'.

Formats spoken single-dash command-line flags such as 'git checkout dash b', 'git commit dash m', 'rm dash rf', 'ls dash la', and 'pytest dash v' into 'git checkout -b', 'git commit -m', 'rm -rf', 'ls -la', and 'pytest -v'.

entries.title: Joins 4-letter split acronyms and more developer terms across speech engines
highlights: Combines 4-part split acronyms and technical names like 'g r p c', 'u u i d', 'c o r s', 'fast a p i', and 'tailwind c s s' into 'gRPC', 'UUID', 'CORS', 'FastAPI', and 'TailwindCSS' when cross-checking both speech engines.
Expands built-in recognition for cloud, database, and developer terms including 'Kubernetes', 'Cloudflare', 'Supabase', 'Vercel', 'Redis', 'SQLite', 'CocoaPods', and 'VoiceOver'.

entries.title: Cleans up two-word mid-thought restarts and speeds up phrase repetition checks
highlights: Collapses mid-sentence restarts where you pause after a two-word connector like 'to the' or 'on the' and repeat the start of your phrase ('We should ship to the we should ship the update tomorrow' becomes 'We should ship the update tomorrow').
Uses fast in-memory buffers during phrase stutter and voice activity checks so short and medium dictations avoid extra memory allocations.

entries.title: Formats spoken IPv4 addresses, API and file paths, and 'v1.2.0' version tags
highlights: Turns spoken local and network IPv4 addresses like '127 dot 0 dot 0 dot 1 colon 8080', '192 dot 168 dot 1 dot 1', and '10 dot 0 dot 0 dot 1 slash 24' into '127.0.0.1:8080', '192.168.1.1', and '10.0.0.1/24'.

Formats spoken API routes, Unix paths, and version tags such as 'slash api slash v1 slash users', 'slash etc slash hosts', 'src slash components slash button dot tsx', and 'v 1 point 2 point 0' into '/api/v1/users', '/etc/hosts', 'src/components/button.tsx', and 'v1.2.0'.

entries.title: Restores casing on cloud, '.js' framework, and Apple developer names
highlights: Formats spoken '.js' framework names and cloud services including 'Next.js' (whether spoken as 'nextjs' or 'next dot js'), 'Vue.js', 'Node.js', 'Nuxt.js', 'NestJS', 'Three.js', 'TailwindCSS', 'Kubernetes', 'Cloudflare', 'Supabase', 'Vercel', 'Netlify', 'Firebase', 'Redis', 'SQLite', and 'gRPC'.
Restores official capitalization on Apple developer tools and platforms including 'iPadOS', 'Xcode', 'TestFlight', 'CocoaPods', and 'VoiceOver'.

entries.title: Hyphenates spoken modifiers like 'open-source', 'cross-platform', and 'built-in'
highlights: Adds hyphens to common technical modifiers before their nouns, turning 'open source library', 'cross platform support', 'built in cache', 'client side validation', 'server side rendering', 'in memory store', 'low latency streaming', 'high priority bug', and 'long running session' into hyphenated compounds.
Keeps normal phrases like 'built in Swift' or 'kept in memory' unchanged without hyphens.

entries.title: Formats spoken Japanese yen and latency units like 'ms', 'µs', and 'kbps'
highlights: Formats spoken yen amounts such as '5,000 yen' and '10 million yen' into '¥5,000' and '¥10 million'.

Abbreviates spoken latency and audio bitrate measurements after numbers, turning '188.5 milliseconds', '45 microseconds', '10 nanoseconds', and '64 kilobits per second' into '188.5 ms', '45 µs', '10 ns', and '64 kbps'.

entries.title: Formats spoken environment variables and underscore code names
highlights: Turns spoken underscore identifiers like 'max underscore retries' and 'user underscore id' into 'max_retries' and 'user_id', and uppercases well-known environment variables like 'node underscore env' and 'gemini underscore api underscore key' into 'NODE_ENV' and 'GEMINI_API_KEY'.
Leaves normal sentences that use 'underscore' as a verb untouched.

entries.title: Smarter Custom Words learning for dotted tech names and possessive names
highlights: When you edit spoken words into dotted, slashed, or hyphenated names like 'Next.js', 'Vue.js', or 'CI/CD' after pasting, GeminiFlow now recognizes the full name and offers to remember it in Custom Words.
When you fix the spelling of a possessive name like 'Owen's' to 'Eoin's', GeminiFlow automatically learns the base name ('Owen' to 'Eoin') so future dictations match both forms.

entries.title: Cleaner dictation inside and right after parentheses and brackets
highlights: When you place your cursor inside empty parentheses or square brackets and dictate a note, GeminiFlow keeps the first word lowercase and leaves out the extra period and trailing space before the closing bracket.
Adds a leading space and lowercases continuing words when you dictate immediately after a closing parenthesis or bracket mid-sentence.

entries.title: Formats spoken pull requests, issue numbers, and platform version numbers
highlights: Turns spoken references like 'pull request 42', 'PR 105', 'issue number 108', 'ticket number 512', and 'bug number 79' into 'PR #42', 'PR #105', 'issue #108', 'ticket #512', and 'bug #79'.
Formats spoken version numbers after platform and tool names such as 'iOS 18 point 2', 'macOS 15 point 1', and 'Python 3 point 12 point 1' into 'iOS 18.2', 'macOS 15.1', and 'Python 3.12.1'.

entries.title: Formats spoken keyboard shortcuts like 'Cmd+Shift+P' and 'Ctrl+C'
highlights: Turns spoken keyboard shortcuts such as 'command shift P', 'command option escape', 'press command A', 'command C', 'command V', and 'control C' into 'Cmd+Shift+P', 'Cmd+Opt+Esc', 'press Cmd+A', 'Cmd+C', 'Cmd+V', and 'Ctrl+C'.
Leaves ordinary sentences like 'command a large fleet' or 'control a remote system' untouched.

entries.title: Faster settings and combined vocabulary lookup across dictations
highlights: Checks whether your rules settings file has changed on disk before reading it, avoiding repeat file reads when your settings are unchanged.
Reuses the combined vocabulary list in memory when neither your Custom Words nor your rules file has changed.

entries.title: Formats spoken dotfiles like '.env' and '.gitignore' and more terminal commands
highlights: Turns spoken dotfiles like 'dot env', 'dot env dot local', 'dot gitignore', 'dot zshrc', and 'dot npmrc' into '.env', '.env.local', '.gitignore', '.zshrc', and '.npmrc', and adds support for shell, Protobuf, GraphQL, SQLite, and Xcode project extensions.
Keeps more spoken command-line tools in lowercase when dictating into code editors and terminals, including 'swift', 'gh', 'uv', 'bun', 'pnpm', 'terraform', 'kubectl', and 'gcloud'.

entries.title: Formats spoken euros, pounds, and computing units like 'GB', 'Mbps', and 'kHz'
highlights: Formats spoken euro and pound amounts such as '20 euros and 50 cents', '3.5 million euros', '25 pounds and 50 pence', and '100 million pounds' into '€20.50', '€3.5 million', '£25.50', and '£100 million'.

Abbreviates spoken technical units after numbers, turning '16 gigabytes', '500 megabytes', '100 megabits per second', '16 kilohertz', '2.4 gigahertz', and '60 frames per second' into '16 GB', '500 MB', '100 Mbps', '16 kHz', '2.4 GHz', and '60 fps'.

entries.title: Formats spoken web links, URL paths, and developer brand names
highlights: Turns spoken web addresses and local server paths such as 'https colon slash slash docs dot github dot com slash en slash actions' and 'http colon slash slash localhost colon 3000 slash api slash v1' into clean links.

Restores proper capitalization on developer and tech names including 'TypeScript', 'JavaScript', 'GraphQL', 'PostgreSQL', 'MongoDB', 'FastAPI', 'PyTorch', 'OpenAI', 'DeepSeek', 'GitLab', 'SwiftUI', and 'WebSocket'.

entries.title: Skips disk reads when your Custom Words file has not changed
highlights: Checks the file modification timestamp on your Custom Words list before reading from disk, avoiding repeat file reads on every dictation when your list is unchanged.
Reuses the prepared vocabulary and replacement pair lists in memory across turns.

entries.title: Cleans up 'oops', 'whoops', and 'my bad' self-corrections and tech environment swaps
highlights: Recognizes natural self-correction cues like 'oops', 'whoops', 'my bad', and 'oh my bad' ('Send it on Monday, my bad, Tuesday' becomes 'Send it on Tuesday').
Handles quick swaps between technical environments and modes such as 'Deploy to staging, sorry, production' and 'Update the frontend, wait, backend'.

entries.title: Cleans up contraction stutters like 'I'm I am' and 'we're we are'
highlights: When you start a word as a contraction and immediately repeat it in full ('I'm I am going to ship it', 'we're we are ready', 'it's it is working', or 'don't do not touch that'), GeminiFlow keeps only the resolved phrase.
Also cleans up the reverse restart ('I am I'm going to ship it' to 'I'm going to ship it').

entries.title: Joins more split software terms like 'webhook', 'dashboard', and 'pipeline'
highlights: Combines developer terms that speech recognizers often split into two words, including 'web hook', 'key chain', 'hot key', 'life cycle', 'middle ware', 'meta data', 'frame work', 'sand box', 'screen shot', 'pipe line', 'dash board', 'bench mark', 'dead lock', 'host name', 'user name', 'pass word', 'file name', and 'byte code'.
Cross-checks these compound terms across both speech engines so your technical dictations stay clean.

entries.title: Faster vocabulary and word-replacement caching during text cleanup
highlights: Caches your cleaned custom vocabulary list and pre-built replacement patterns in memory when your settings files have not changed.
Skips compound-word cleanup checks when a sentence does not contain any matching stems.

entries.title: Automatic log rotation during long-running sessions
highlights: Rotates the diagnostic log file automatically during long-running dictation sessions whenever it reaches 5 MB, instead of only checking when the app starts.
Protects log timestamp formatting when background network tasks and the main app log at the same time.

entries.title: Smarter question marks for negative questions, 'What's', and tag questions
highlights: Adds a question mark reliably on negative questions ('Can't we meet at 3:00 p.m.?', 'Don't you think we should wait?'), contracted questions ('What's the plan for 3:00 p.m.?', 'How's the release going?'), 'What if' and 'Which' questions, and tag questions ('We are still meeting at 3:00 p.m., aren't we?', 'You updated the baseline, didn't you?').
Keeps imperative sentences like 'Do the migration tomorrow.' and 'Have a great weekend.' as statements with a period.

entries.title: Improves British accent and technical phrase recognition on-device
highlights: Repairs common on-device mishearings on British and fast voices such as 'fixed the bag' ('fixed the bug'), 'feels really Rispo' ('feels really responsive'), and 'off the laptop link to sleep' ('after the laptop wakes from sleep').
Preserves ordinary phrases like 'carry the bag' or 'in the bag' untouched.

entries.title: Hyphenates spoken technical modifiers like 'end-to-end' and 'real-time'
highlights: Formats spoken compound modifiers before their nouns, turning 'end to end tests', 'real time audio', 'read only mode', 'command line tool', 'out of the box support', 'zero downtime deployment', 'on call rotation', and 'hands on workshop' into 'end-to-end tests', 'real-time audio', 'read-only mode', 'command-line tool', 'out-of-the-box support', 'zero-downtime deployment', 'on-call rotation', and 'hands-on workshop'.
Leaves standalone phrases like 'from end to end' or 'in real time' unchanged.

entries.title: Faster Custom Words lookup and replacement matching
highlights: Caches your Custom Words list in memory between dictations when the file on disk has not changed, avoiding repeat file parsing on every sentence.
Reuses compiled matching patterns when applying 'When you hear X, write Y' word replacements.

entries.title: Fixes 'defer loading' and 'settings screen' phrasing across speech engines
highlights: Repairs 'differ loading' or 'differ rendering' to 'defer loading' and 'defer rendering' when followed by an action word, while keeping real comparisons like 'differ from the baseline' untouched.

Restores the dropped plural in 'the setting screen' or 'user setting menu' ('the settings screen', 'user settings menu') and keeps capitalized compound words like 'Code Base' formatted cleanly as 'Codebase'.

entries.title: More reliable background finishing for multi-part live dictations
highlights: When a long dictation with multiple speech segments finishes in the background while you start a new press, GeminiFlow now tracks each segment's completion echo and covered audio position individually.
Prevents an earlier segment's completion signal from ending the final segment early.

entries.title: Joins split software compound words and fixes 'first, then on' phrasing
highlights: Combines software compound words that speech recognizers often split apart, turning 'mock ups', 'code base', 'work flow', 'end point', 'time stamp', 'name space', 'data base', 'change log', and 'tool chain' into 'mockups', 'codebase', 'workflow', 'endpoint', 'timestamp', 'namespace', 'database', 'changelog', and 'toolchain'.
Fixes 'on reliability first thing on speed' to 'on reliability first, then on speed' while keeping real schedule phrases like 'first thing on Monday' untouched.

entries.title: Smarter Custom Words learning for 3-letter acronyms and capitalization edits
highlights: When you edit spaced letters like 'L L M' or 'S Q L' into 'LLM' or 'SQL' after pasting, GeminiFlow now recognizes the 3-word edit and offers to remember it in Custom Words.
Ignores simple first-letter capitalization changes on ordinary words ('meeting' to 'Meeting') while still learning real mixed-case brand and tech edits ('graphql' to 'GraphQL').

entries.title: Recovers compound tech names and two-word Custom Words across both speech engines
highlights: When Apple's on-device listener recognizes a compound technical name or Custom Word like 'WebSocket', 'SwiftUI', 'PostgreSQL', or 'GeminiFlow' where the cloud transcript split it into two words ('web socket', 'Gemini flow'), GeminiFlow merges it into the proper spelling automatically.
Also cross-checks two-word Custom Words ('Agent Studio') against Apple's on-device transcript when the surrounding sentence matches.

entries.title: Finishes background live dictations faster when the final pause has no speech
highlights: When you start a second dictation right after releasing the first and the first dictation's final turn closes with only silence or a key click after earlier speech, GeminiFlow now finishes the first dictation immediately in 0.15 seconds instead of waiting 1.5 seconds.
If the first dictation had no earlier text, it switches to the backup transcription service right away instead of waiting out the full timeout.

entries.title: Smarter mid-sentence cursor spacing and natural 'Scratch that' voice undo phrases
highlights: Improves mid-sentence dictation continuation when inserting a new sentence before continuing text or when the text after your cursor has no leading space.
Recognizes natural voice undo phrases such as 'Oops, scratch that, please', 'Oh, sorry, undo the last sentence', and 'Wait, delete last dictation'.

entries.title: Protects live audio streaming against uneven sample boundaries on reconnects
highlights: Ensures every live audio chunk, reconnect resend, and planned session rotation stays aligned on exact 16-bit audio sample boundaries and within the recorded audio buffer.
Prevents audio clicks or range errors if a network reconnect or turn split resumes from an uneven byte offset.

entries.title: Formats spoken filenames, slash compounds, and command-line flags
highlights: Turns spoken developer and document filenames like 'main dot m', 'package dot json', 'readme dot md', 'index dot ts', and 'report dot pdf' into 'main.m', 'package.json', 'README.md', 'index.ts', and 'report.pdf'.

Formats spoken slash expressions and command-line flags such as 'and slash or', 'yes slash no', 'CI slash CD', 'TCP slash IP', 'I slash O', 'dash dash help', and 'dash dash dry run' into 'and/or', 'yes/no', 'CI/CD', 'TCP/IP', 'I/O', '--help', and '--dry-run'.

entries.title: Refreshes the microphone automatically when your Mac wakes from sleep
highlights: Detects when your Mac wakes from sleep while GeminiFlow is idle and refreshes the audio input engine right away.
Prevents the first dictation after opening your laptop lid from hitting a stale microphone connection or waiting for an automatic retry.

entries.title: Shared iOS and Mac support for app-aware formatting, mid-sentence continuation, and voice undo
highlights: Extends app-aware formatting to recognize popular iOS email, chat, and terminal apps alongside Mac apps.
Adds cross-platform engine hooks so iOS keyboards and host apps can supply surrounding cursor text for mid-sentence lowercase continuation and handle 'Scratch that' voice undo automatically.

entries.title: Queues on-device audio file fallback when a new dictation is already recording
highlights: When an earlier dictation falls back to Apple's on-device audio file recognizer while you are already speaking a new dictation, GeminiFlow now waits until you release the key before running the file recognizer so the two never compete for the on-device speech engine.
Preserves your exact dictation order by processing the queued recording right before delivering deferred pastes.

entries.title: Zero-warning macOS 27 build and online slow split-turn test verification
highlights: Updates audio tap compilation so GeminiFlow builds cleanly with zero compiler warnings on the latest macOS 27 SDK.
Adds an online test mode to simulate slow mid-dictation turn responses and verify that no spoken words are dropped while waiting.

entries.title: Finishes rapid back-to-back dictations in parallel on Gemini Live
highlights: When you release Fn and immediately start a new dictation before the previous one finishes, GeminiFlow now keeps the previous live connection open in the background for up to 1.5 seconds while starting a fresh connection for your new press.
Delivers the first dictation in a fraction of a second without having to re-send its entire audio recording to the slower backup service.

entries.title: Fixes 'bill' vs 'build' in software phrases and formats spoken versions and ports
highlights: When you dictate software phrases like 'ship the new build' or 'deploy the staging build', GeminiFlow now writes 'build' instead of 'bill', while leaving everyday sentences like 'pay the bill' or 'I have a bill tomorrow' untouched.

Formats spoken software version numbers and local ports such as 'version 2 point 4', 'version 1 point 0 point 2', 'localhost colon 3000', and 'port 80 80' into 'version 2.4', 'version 1.0.2', 'localhost:3000', and 'port 8080'.

entries.title: Faster backup transcription on long dictations and protection for recordings over 8 minutes
highlights: When a long dictation needs the backup transcription service after most of your speech was already confirmed live, GeminiFlow now sends only the unfinished tail and stitches it seamlessly onto the confirmed text.
Caps inline backup audio safely under Google's 20 MB request limit so recordings longer than 8 minutes never fail with an oversized payload error.

entries.title: Connects to Gemini Live while the microphone starts and stops waiting sooner after you let go
highlights: Starts the Gemini Live connection at the exact moment you press Fn in parallel with starting the microphone and status pill, cutting 65 to 350 milliseconds off connection setup on short presses.
Stops the post-release audio cushion as soon as your microphone captures quiet audio past the key release instead of always waiting the full 120 milliseconds.

entries.title: Mid-sentence continuation after deleting words, 'oh sorry' self-corrections, and date formatting
highlights: On Mac, when you delete a word and restart dictation in the middle of a sentence, GeminiFlow now continues with a lowercase word and matching spacing instead of starting with a capital letter.

Catches 'oh sorry' and 'sorry' mid-thought course corrections (such as 'I want to go at two, oh sorry, hey, I want to go at three') even when there is a pause before or after 'oh sorry', and formats spoken dates and phone numbers.

entries.title: Formats spoken email addresses, web domains, and tech brand names
highlights: Turns spoken email addresses and websites like 'sarah at acme dot com' and 'docs dot github dot com' into 'sarah@acme.com' and 'docs.github.com' while leaving normal sentences like 'look at example.com' intact.
Automatically capitalizes tech brand names like iPhone, iPad, iMac, iCloud, macOS, AirPods, MacBook, GitHub, and YouTube.

entries.title: Keeps words spoken across mid-dictation turn splits without gaps or duplicates
highlights: When the live server closes a speech turn while you are still talking, GeminiFlow re-sends the last fraction of a second of audio into the next turn so words in flight are never clipped.
Automatically removes any repeated boundary words when stitching live speech segments together.

entries.title: Finishes 10-minute hands-free dictations smoothly even if the session expires at release
highlights: If Google's 10-minute live session limit is reached right after you stop a long hands-free dictation, GeminiFlow keeps everything transcribed so far and finishes only the last few seconds on a fresh live connection.
Avoids falling back to re-sending the entire 10-minute recording from scratch when only the final sentence is still pending.

entries.title: Keeps back-to-back dictations cleanly separated and protects the status pill
highlights: When you finish one dictation and immediately start another, leftover audio from the first press can no longer spill into the start of the new recording.
Prevents a background API key check from covering the status pill while a dictation is still finishing, and removes unused internal session state.

entries.title: Faster text cleanup and smoother installs on Apple M1 Macs
highlights: Skips unnecessary text cleanup passes when a sentence has no numbers, spoken line breaks, or extra filler phrases, cutting text polish time significantly.
Fixes a self-test speed check that could block install.sh and update.sh on Apple M1 Macs under normal background load (GitHub issue #1).

entries.title: Learns new custom words when you fix a spelling after pasting
highlights: When you manually fix the spelling of a name or special term right after pasting ('Shavon' to 'Siobhan' or 'Zebra' to 'Zyphra'), GeminiFlow notices the edit and offers a one-click 'Remember in Custom Words' item in the menu bar.
Ignores ordinary sentence edits and common words so it only suggests real names, brands, and technical terms.

entries.title: Formats spoken currencies, percentages, temperatures, and question marks naturally
highlights: Turns spoken numbers like '20 dollars and 50 cents', '$3.5 million dollars', '25.5 percent', '98.6 degrees', '1920 by 1080', and 'from 2 to 3 p.m.' into clean '$20.50', '$3.5 million', '25.5%', '98.6°', '1920x1080', and '2-3 p.m.' automatically.
Adds a question mark reliably when a question ends with 'a.m.' or 'p.m.' ('Can we meet at 3:00 p.m.?') or after a mid-sentence self-correction.

entries.title: Say 'Scratch that' to undo your last paste and protect against window switches
highlights: If you say 'Scratch that' or 'Undo that' right after a dictation is pasted, GeminiFlow removes the text it just typed instead of pasting the words 'Scratch that'.
If you switch to a different app before a dictation finishes, GeminiFlow copies the text safely to your clipboard instead of pasting into the wrong window.

entries.title: Finishes dictation right away when you pause before letting go of Fn
highlights: Watches the last fraction of a second of audio before you release the key and skips the extra 120ms wait when you have already finished speaking.
Keeps the full safety cushion whenever you are still speaking as you let go, so your last syllable is never cut off.

entries.title: Combines both speech engines to catch small skipped words
highlights: Cross-checks Google's cloud transcript with Apple's on-device listener at the moment you release the key, with zero extra wait.
Recovers quick connecting words like 'a', 'the', and 'to' that can get swallowed in fast speech, and prefers your Custom Words when the two engines hear a sound-alike differently.

entries.title: Adapts formatting to the app you are typing in
highlights: In email apps like Mail, Superhuman, Mimestream, and Outlook, greetings and sign-offs are spaced onto their own paragraphs automatically.
In chat apps like Slack, Messages, Discord, and WhatsApp, short one-sentence replies skip the trailing period, while code editors and terminals keep command names in lowercase.

entries.title: Turns spoken lists into clean numbered and bulleted lists
highlights: Say 'First, ... Second, ... Third, ...' or 'Number one, ... Number two, ...' and GeminiFlow formats your items as a numbered list on separate lines.
Say 'bullet point' or 'next bullet' before each item to create a clean bulleted list without touching ordinary sentences.

entries.title: Clearer recognition when speaking softly or using AirPods
highlights: Automatically boosts quiet speech on Mac and iPhone when you speak in a low voice or use AirPods and Bluetooth headsets.
Leaves normal speech, silence, and background room sounds untouched so nothing unwanted is picked up.

entries.title: Cleans up mid-sentence self-corrections when you change your mind
highlights: When you correct yourself out loud ('Meet at two, wait no, three p.m.' or 'invite Alice and, wait no, Bob and Carol'), GeminiFlow keeps only what you meant to say.
Understands natural backtrack phrases such as 'wait no', 'actually no', 'scratch that', 'sorry I meant', and 'or rather' while leaving everyday conversation untouched.

entries.title: Faster text cleanup at the end of every dictation
highlights: Keeps your text cleanup rules ready in memory instead of reloading them each time you speak.
Polishes and pastes your finished text almost instantly while using less battery.

entries.title: Apple on-device speech recognizes your Custom Words
highlights: Your custom words and replacement targets ('Siobhan', 'Eoin') are now provided to Apple's on-device speech recognizer with each dictation.
Improves on-device transcription accuracy and offline fallback when you speak names, technical terms, and custom vocabulary.

entries.title: Faster fallback when a connection drops mid-sentence
highlights: If a network glitch interrupts sending audio to Google's speech model, GeminiFlow catches the error immediately instead of waiting for a timeout.
During a dictation it reconnects and resumes from where it left off, and if you have already released the key it falls back to the safety net right away.

entries.title: Custom Words: replacement pairs ('Owen -> Eoin')
highlights: Teach GeminiFlow how to replace words you say with the spelling you want: type a pair such as 'Owen -> Eoin' directly in the Custom Words window (or enter it in custom-words.json).
Replaces whole words and phrases across all transcription engines ('Owen' and 'Owen's' change; 'Owens' and 'Bowen' stay untouched) and biases the spelling in Gemini Live.

entries.title: Custom Words: names and unusual terms spelled your way
highlights: A list of up to 100 names and unusual terms is sent to Google's speech model with each dictation so it writes them the way you do (in testing 'Shavon' became 'Siobhan'). If the service ever refuses the list, dictation carries on without it.

On the Mac, edit the list from the Custom Words menu item. It is stored outside the project folder and applies from your next dictation. Keep it to names and unusual terms: a listed everyday word replaces its sound-alikes.

entries.title: Sturdier Setup, Changelog and API key windows
highlights: First run asks for Speech Recognition and the microphone at the right moments, the API key box only accepts something that looks like a key and shows the saved key masked, and closing a window hands you back to the app you were typing in.

Buttons need a press and release on the same spot, the search box clears with its X or Esc, long changelog titles no longer overlap, VoiceOver can read both windows, and test runs no longer flash extra icons in the menu bar.
An update no longer restarts the app while you are dictating: it waits until your text has been delivered.

entries.title: Long dictations stay on Live when the last sound is only a click or a breath
highlights: After a pause in a long dictation, a key click or breath just before release no longer throws away the text Live already returned and sends the whole recording to the slower backup.
The text is finished on Live only when the audio after the last answered part has no speech in it; anything that could be a word still goes to the backup, so nothing said is lost.

entries.title: Repeated phrases and mid-thought restarts cleaned up
highlights: Keeps one copy when a phrase is said twice in a row while you gather a thought ('with my with my new app', 'I would I would', 'will do will do'), and when you restart after one dropped word ('I also want you to give some I also want you to give updates').
Leaves deliberate repeats alone: emphasis after a comma ('I know, I know'), courtesy phrases, names, number runs and idioms such as 'again and again'. Runs on your Mac in well under a millisecond.

entries.title: Brand refresh shared with GeminiFlow for iOS & cleaner windows
highlights: Adopted the iOS brand mark (three slanted bars) for the menu bar icon and the in-app icon, and the GeminiFlow wordmark typography in window headers.
Moved the Changelog and Setup titles below the window buttons and removed the trailing dots from menu items and buttons.

entries.title: Mac-native Changelog (Cmd+L), closable Setup window (Cmd+P) & iOS sync
highlights: Added a clean, flat Mac-native Changelog window (Cmd+L, Cmd+W, Esc) with inline titlebar search, Engine filter, collapsible timeline, and canonical changelog.json for iOS sync.

Replaced the modal Permissions alert with a closable Setup & Permissions window (Cmd+P) featuring live API key, Microphone, Accessibility, Speech, and Fn-key status indicators plus API key paste sanitization.

entries.title: Silent-press prompt-echo guard & low-evidence silence net
highlights: Stopped silent presses with 1 to 4 stray on-device noise characters from pasting echoed REST instructions ('Transcribe and clean up this audio dictation.').
Instructed the REST fallback model to return an empty result on silence or background noise and routed empty low-evidence responses cleanly to No speech.

entries.title: Noise-relative silence detection & REST plausibility safety net
highlights: Measured speech evidence relative to each press's 20th-percentile room noise floor so quiet-room taps and holds end immediately as No speech instead of calling REST.
Added a numbers-only REST plausibility net rejecting hallucinated zero-timestamps ('00:00') and runaway text lengths on silent audio.

entries.title: Zero word loss across slow split turns
highlights: Held voiced audio (with 0.3s pre-roll) behind any in-flight split turn until generationComplete arrives instead of reopening early after 1.5s, eliminating dropped seam words.
Raised the T26 multi-close hands-free recall gate from 0.95 to 0.99.

entries.title: Hands-free HUD indicator redesign
highlights: Replaced the outer mint rim and glow in locked hands-free mode with a crisp 7px green indicator dot on a soft inner halo and solid green waveform bars inside the pill.
Kept hold-to-talk, Thinking, and notice pill renders pixel-identical.

entries.title: Planned Live session rotation before the 10-minute server cap
highlights: Proactively rotates the Gemini Live WebSocket at the first quiet split point after 8.5 minutes with zero resent audio and zero seam duplicates.
Treats server closes after 9.5 minutes (or after goAway) as planned rotations that do not consume the 2-reconnect drop budget.

entries.title: Accurate 4-gram duplicate-phrase test gate
highlights: Updated duplicated_phrases() in the test runner to flag 4-grams only when they appear at least twice in the output and more often than in expected text, eliminating false positives on minor recognizer phrasing variants.

entries.title: 5- and 10-minute marathon dictation suite & privacy-safe press stats
highlights: Added opt-in 5-minute and 10-minute continuous Live dictation gates (T23) and scaled the e2e watchdog for multi-minute sessions.
Logged one numbers-only Press stats line per dictation (audio duration, Live session age, reconnects, and activity count).

entries.title: Visual distinction for locked hands-free HUD & offscreen PNG renderer
highlights: Added visual differentiation between hold-to-talk and double-tap locked hands-free mode on the floating HUD pill.
Added --render-hud-png for deterministic 2x offscreen HUD verification.

entries.title: Release-cushion telemetry & atomic test audio cache
highlights: Logged numbers-only Fn-up release cushion coverage (hostTime reach past key release and post-release RMS) to measure real hardware buffer lag.
Made test runner TTS and WAV cache writes atomic so interrupted runs never leave truncated audio fixtures.

entries.title: Instant completion when releasing Fn between Live turns
highlights: Finished Live dictations immediately on key release (~135ms instead of ~570ms) when all prior speech was already finalized at a pause split and no uncovered speech remains.

entries.title: Last-sentence question punctuation & filler-like cleanup
highlights: Judged trailing '?' vs '.' from the final sentence rather than earlier clauses in multi-sentence dictations.
Removed stray filler 'like' immediately preceding a stripped 'kind of' or 'sort of' hedge.

entries.title: Context-aware 'kind of' and 'sort of' filler removal
highlights: Stripped 'kind of' and 'sort of' only when set off as spoken pauses or adjacent to vocal fillers, preserving meaningful uses like 'what kind of car' and 'sort of works'.

entries.title: Pronoun capitalization, mixed-case brands & grammatical doubles
highlights: Protected 'i.e.', dotfiles ('.env'), URLs, and mixed-case names ('iPhone', 'macOS') during capitalization and punctuation cleanup.
Collapsed single-word stutters ('the the', 'I I') while keeping grammatical doubles ('had had', 'that that', 'very very').

entries.title: Header-only API key auth & automatic log redaction
highlights: Moved Gemini API key authentication from query URLs into the x-goog-api-key request header across Live WebSocket and REST calls.
Added defensive secret scrubbing in GFLog and static binary/request verification (T19).
